segmentation.text: shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
or the directions of a police officer
in any of the following places:
Alongside or opposite any highway excavation or obstruction
when stopping, standing or parking would obstruct traffic.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

st.obstruction is "a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind ∈ {debris, excavation, hose, barrier, stalled_vehicle_wreckage, sidewalk_fixture, mail_drop_box, other}": "excavation" is its kind excavation and "obstruction" every kind of it. "highway" places it on the way the vehicle is on: the object lies on a highway (st.on_way: "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"; st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines" as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it) whose extent the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). The vehicle is alongside or opposite it where the object lies to the vehicle's side, beside it or across the way, rather than ahead or behind: its signed lateral offset (prim.region_lateral_offset: "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user") is nonzero and the ground distance from the vehicle's body to it (st.region_geometry) is at most the magnitude of that offset. st.on_way is not read as nearness, st.region_geometry not as occupancy, and st.highway not as the roadway.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

operationalizations.standard: stopping, standing or parking would obstruct traffic
operationalizations.convention: the free lateral width one passing vehicle needs beside a standing vehicle (design-vehicle width with its lateral clearance): a halt beside or opposite an excavation or obstruction obstructs traffic where neither the gap between the vehicle's body and the object nor the gap between its body and the roadway edge on its other side leaves that width

applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation there is an obstruction o (st.obstruction, of any kind) lying on a highway h (st.on_way) whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies), such that o's signed lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset) is nonzero and the ground distance from the subject's body to o (st.region_geometry) is at most the magnitude of that offset (o to the subject's side, beside it or across the way), and a halt there would obstruct traffic: the ground distance from the subject's body to o is less than p.free_passage_width, and no roadway edge e (st.road_edge) whose signed lateral offset from the subject is of the sign opposite to o's lies at a ground distance from the subject's body of at least p.free_passage_width.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject is at rest there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.

"would obstruct traffic" is read as the passage traffic needs, whether or not a member of traffic is present (the words state what the halt would do): the free width between the vehicle and the object and between the vehicle and the roadway edge on its other side. A passage beyond the far side of the object, away from the vehicle, is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A st.obstruction of kind excavation lies on the highway in the right lane; the subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, is at rest (kin.speed zero) in the left lane alongside it, its body 0.3 m from the excavation and 0.5 m from the left st.road_edge; no other road user, no human direction and no device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject moves past the excavation at kin.speed 6 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is at rest beside the excavation with its body 0.3 m from it and 4.5 m of roadway between its body and the road edge on its other side, so the halt leaves a passage.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source maps the regions without their outlines, so every distance and lateral offset to them is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The excavation lies against the right curb; the subject is at rest against the left road edge directly across from it, its body 2 m from the excavation and 0.3 m from the left edge.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs the subject's lane.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source's kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: jam spacing of halted vehicles in traffic-flow studies (Highway Capacity Manual)

param_proposals.name: p.free_passage_width
param_proposals.convention: the free lateral width one passing vehicle needs beside a standing vehicle: the width of a design passenger or single-unit vehicle with its lateral clearance, about a narrow traffic lane
param_proposals.source: AASHTO design vehicle widths and lane widths (Green Book)
